utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in the courtroom, and especially good morning, Ms. Frease, again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, yesterday you finished your cross-examination, but perhaps there are -- during night-time, you -- during night-time you had, like Mr. Vanderpuye indicated yesterday, that there's some additional questions, or was that completed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everybody. May God's peace reign in this house and may God's will be done and not necessarily mine in these proceedings. Your Honours, thank you for giving me the floor. I would like to inform you that my cross-examination is completed. I would like to thank you and everybody who has assisted me with the cross-examination of this witness and also I would like to thank the witness, once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye, your cross-examination -- your re-examination. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Good morning to you, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Ms. Frease. I apologise for having you back here again today. I have really just three areas that I wanted to cover on re-direct examination so I'll get right to it. What I wanted to have you look at is this binder here. It contains within it P792, and this is the binder of intercepts which I think you'd referred to before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to have that shown to the witness, if I could, please. And then I'd also like to have it shown to the Court, because I think it will be helpful to understand the context of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, could you basically just describe the binder and could you confirm that it is the binder, in fact, that you've been discussing during the course of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the binder that I've been discussing. And one of the unusual features about it that I had forgotten until seeing it again is that it was put together from left to right, so that the holes that were made were made on the right-hand side of the column so that we would lose as little text as possible. If the holes were punched on the left-hand side, we would have lost more text. So we sort of worked from left to right with the material. Yes, I remember this binder well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were asked yesterday, I think it was, some questions about whether or not it contained certain notes or -- or indications?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I'd just ask to you flip through that and see if you see any such notes. There may be some, but there might not be, but I'd just ask to you take a look.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In flipping through it, it doesn't appear that there are any notes on any of the conversations in this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does it appear to be in relatively the same condition as it was when it was received?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does it contain the -- well, does it contain page numbers?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is there an indication in the binder itself? It may be on the last page although I'm not sure as to how many pages it actually contains.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last page says 548 pages, and it runs through ERN number 00728099. And these are handwritten page numbers on the top right corner of each page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know if those numbers were placed there by members of the Tribunal or members of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe when we received these, these were -- these numbers were already here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And does it contain the same indications that you'd mentioned during the course of your testimony with respect to the black marks at the bottom of the page, where certain illegible portions as a result of the photocopying?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that present intermittently or is it present throughout the binder?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be present throughout binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does that comport with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't have any more questions with respect to this document. I would, however, like to, as we say back home, publish this, that is, to have the Court examine it should the Court desire to see it. I think it's -- it's a very probative of the witness's testimony and I think it will help the Court understand the circumstances that the witness was talking about in relation to the analysis of this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Vanderpuye, the Chamber would like to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the Defence should have the chance to look at it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. I have already shown it to Mr. Gajic, although I have not shown it yet to Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't need to see it. Mr. Gajic has seen it. Thank you. If Mr. Gajic has seen it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, did you see it? Have you had the chance to look at this binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just briefly for some 15 seconds or so. Therefore, I would really like to have a better look at it, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will give you the opportunity to do that. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber had, I think, 30 seconds to look at it, but it appears that the last page has the number 00728100. The witness saw the -- the second-last page as the last, but there's no other difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. 8100 is the last page, and I believe that particular document indicates the number of pages that are in the binder and is stamped as well. It is very faint. I think we saw it in e-court a couple of days ago. But I believe that's -- that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the first number appears to be 00727551. Thank you. The binder should be given to Mr. Gajic. While Mr. Gajic is looking at it, I think you may proceed and continue your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, I wanted to refer you to a memo. That is P863. That is a memo from Peter Nicholson to Mr. Ruez. I think you commented on it. It's dated 18 -- oh, maybe I have the wrong number. P811. And that's dated 18 December 1998, and it -- it is a memo from Peter Nicholson and Rick Butler to Mr. Ruez. Do you remember commenting about that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd need you to refresh my recollection. I do remember the memo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. In particular, you were asked about the circumstances under which the notebooks of the 2nd Corps intercepts or the intercepts taken by the 2nd Corps were found and in particular you remarked -- if I may refresh your recollection, on page 5254 of the transcript, you remarked as follows. A question was put to you by Mr. Tolimir. "My question to you is: Did you check these registration numbers on the notebooks, because I've seen here that some of them do not have numbers, and can you tell us what could be the reason why they would be marked and treated as official documents and documentation and later burned?" And your answer was: "The only thing I remember is that when the members of the Office of the Prosecutor first found the notebooks at the northern site, that the ABiH person with them was embarrassed that they were not kept in an orderly manner and then he also said, Actually we shouldn't have these anymore." Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And what I'd like to do is just to refer to you, if I could, to page 2 of this document. Okay. And if you look to the -- I guess it would be the fourth paragraph, fourth full paragraph anyway. You can see it begins with: "They were located in a locked wooden cabinet in the basement," referring to the notebooks. And then after you can see the next sentence, I guess it's the thirds sentence, it says: "In fact they were just haphazardly placed in the cabinet and did not look as if they had been touched in years. And then an ABiH official explained in an embarrassed manner that the logs should not even be here at this stage." Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what I'd like to show you is, a couple of photographs that were attended to this memo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could show 65 ter 6539.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: While that is loading, can I ask you, do you have a specific recollection of how the notebooks were found or where they were found?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just for the record, the original binder was given back to the Prosecution. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you seen this photograph before, Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. What it's described as in the memo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're right. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the memo itself, in the last paragraph of the second page, it indicates -- it reads as follows: "Upon reaching the wooden locker, we observed that it was open and that all of the documents had been organised and bundled." And then it indicates a series of photos, 1, 2, and 3. Now, have you seen any photographs, I should say, of the locker in which these intercepts were found?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I have, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, and if we could just blow this up a little bit. That would be in the right -- I'm sorry, the left quadrant of the photograph, if could you blow that up a little bit. I think it would be ... the left top, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise any of the documents that you see there in the left-hand side of that photograph, that pile of books?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They look like A-5 size notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And they similar to the style, I should say, and quality --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment, please. Mr. Tolimir wants to raise something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. To the Prosecutor's question, the witness said that she never saw this photo, and then she stated that she only has second-hand knowledge of the photo and now she is being asked questions based on the photo having seen photos in the courtroom. I don't think this should be done. Secondly, the Prosecutor mentions intercepted conversations which means that the intercepted conversations were printed after the war, after the photos were seen. These are just handwritten notes in the notebooks and only subsequently were those copied and made into printed intercepted conversations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do appreciate Mr. Tolimir's position. It seems to me that that is his position as a matter of fact in this case. The questions that are put to the witness are completely appropriate since we have already established that the witness has first-hand familiarity with the notebooks themselves, and I'm asking her to identify, if she can, the documents that are depicted in this photograph as distinguished from identifying the photograph itself. And so I think it is a perfectly appropriate avenue of examination, and if the witness can identify them, then she can. If she can't, she can't. I think it's a pretty straightforward issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, if you use this photo for that purpose, if the witness is recognising anything depicted in this photograph, you should continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, are you able to make out -- I think I was asking whether or not these apparent notebooks bear similarity to the notebooks that you handled back in 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stack on the left looks like a stack of A-5 size children's notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And does that fairly describe the materials that were handed over?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you another photograph, if I could. And that's the second photograph. I think it's page 2 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could just zoom in a little bit on the light blue notebook you can see there in the left corner. Maybe a little bit more. Okay. That's not bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise any of the items that you see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- yes. I mean, some of them also appear to be these A-5 size children's notebooks. The one in the foreground, next to the ashtray, looks like one that was -- could have been used during that same period and also the blueish one on the stack, to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I believe that the Prosecutor should phrase his questions differently. He says, Do you recognise the -- this object? And then she says yes, and then she says, I think it's similar. We can't see the contents. We don't see the handwriting. I think that questions could be phrased differently without suggesting that the notebook is indeed the one in question without inspecting its contents, without looking at the handwriting. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, indeed, you should be careful by phrasing your questions. They shouldn't occur as -- or appear as leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would just -- I would just point out that my question was, are you able to recognise any of the items that you see in this photograph, which I don't think -- other than the fact that I'm referring to items, I don't think is leading in any respect to what they are, where they are, or any specific item. But I -- I do take your point and I will be attentive to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Connect your question with the request of the Usher to focus on the light blue item on the left top side of the photograph, then I think it's merely on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you -- well, let me ask you, do you recall how these notebooks were actually transferred, in what condition notebooks were transferred to the members of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were put in a box and sealed until the Office of the Prosecutor took possession of them, once they had been transported from the site to 2 Corps down in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you page 5 -- I may be mistaken. Page 8, I'm sorry. Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A box that Peter Nicholson and a member of the 2 Corps signed their names on after sealing it with the contents, and the contents being the notebooks. So on the subsequent mission in April of 1998, when I was in Tuzla, I was shown this box and saw this box and the notebooks were contained within it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can see on here on this photograph there's a date, 11 March 1998, on the box itself.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that of any particular significance?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the day that the box was sealed. There was also a sense, or maybe a hope on the side of the Office of the Prosecutor, that the -- those documents would be handed over on that day. We didn't find out until the 12th of March that, in fact, the Office of the Prosecutor would need to wait for approval from the Ministry of Defence, I believe it was, from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd just like to show you one other photograph, and that's -- I think it's page 9. Do you recognise what's depicted here?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same box.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender these photographs. I suppose I should do it as we go. They all fall under 65 ter 6539. There are ten of them in all, but I haven't shown the witness all of them. They were all, however -- well, no, I'm sorry. 1 through 6 of them are referred to specifically in P863 -- I'm sorry, P811. That is the memo itself. Photographs 1, 2, and 3 are referred to in this last paragraph -- and 4, I should say, are referred to in the last paragraph of page 2 of the document. And photos 5 and 6 are referred to and indicate the box or refer to -- and the last page, the third page, of the -- of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do realise that P811 as it is in e-court has certain redactions and those redactions I think survived the last trial so that the document could be made public. We do have an unredacted version which I would like to have the Court -- like to -- to be before the Court in addition to the -- to the redacted version, which I suppose we can upload, and perhaps we can designate it A or B of -- of P811 so that's it clear and the Court has full information concerning the participants in this -- in this mission and that are referred to specifically in the -- in the -- in the memo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This document should not be broadcast. If you are now calling it up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's not actually in e-court yet, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... see the purpose of tendering that document if it is not in e-court yet. We have the public redacted version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I will move to my next area and last area, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the course of your cross-examination, it was suggested in a number of ways that the ABiH and Bosnian MUP fabricated the intercept evidence, the suggestion that they perhaps received this information from other sources, the Americans and other -- other countries operating in the area during the war, was made. And, in particular, you were asked a number of questions, including -- and I would refer to page 5250, 3 through 12. The question was put to as follows: "Q. Thank you. What I'm asking you is this: We have seen quotes from the report on Srebrenica of the Dutch Institute for War Documentation. It's a very serious and voluminous analysis which you can read and then make the conclusion that you just made, but my question is: Did the OTP analyse at all how many people were needed on the southern and northern location to be able to monitor the radio network of the Army of Republika Srpska at the time the events in Srebrenica and Zepa -- of the events in Srebrenica and Zepa to intercept them, transcribe them in realtime and put them into notebooks and on paper and pass this on to their immediate superiors and up to the highest level of command?" And your answer was: "No." You were also shown a document which was P -- I'm sorry, D48, and you were read, in part, the following quote: "Nonetheless, an ABiH General claimed that the messages were actually intercepted and analysed in realtime and it was your understanding that they were," that is the ABiH was, "actually able to process intercepts in realtime." Do you recall those parts of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the first part. I do not recall the second part which is quoted as: "Nonetheless an ABiH General claimed that the messages were actually intercepted ..." I don't recall the part about an ABiH General claimed that the messages were actually intercepted and analysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's not your statement. That's a statement from Exhibit D48, which was a document that was put to you by Mr. Tolimir. That's just a quote from the book.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That helps, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, just for the sake of the record, in page 13, line 21, I think it's the wrong reference recorded. It should read page 5250, lines 3 through 12; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That is correct, 5250, 3 through 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, but the 3 was connected to the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, is it your understanding, while the document that was shown to you by Mr. Tolimir spoke about deficiencies in the ability of the Bosnian army to intercept radio and radio relay communications, it did not refer to any specific weaknesses on the part of the VRS in terms of their ability to protect their radio communications? Is it your understanding that the ABiH intercepted VRS communications in realtime, based upon your investigation and based upon the information that you've gotten from talking with operators and so on?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know whether the VRS and in particular the security organ of the VRS was aware that the ABiH had the ability to actually intercept their radio communications?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it appeared so. It came through their responses at times, amongst themselves, that they didn't want to discuss certain subjects over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It should be 65 ter 2600, 2-6-0-0. While this is loading, Ms. Stewart has reminded me that P998, those -- the set of photographs should be under seal, so I would ask for them to be placed under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... one photo should be under seal. Why the whole set?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: They all apparently indicate the location of the site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: More than the other photos than the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. What I'm showing you here is a document, as can you see from the title of it, it's -- it indicates Military Post 7469, Zvornik. It says "Security organ." If we go down to the bottom of the page we can see that it signed by chief of the security, chief of security, Lieutenant Drago Nikolic, is what it says; right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And this is the Drago Nikolic you testified about before in your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I'd like to draw your attention specifically to the first paragraph of this document. You can see that it is dated 22nd April 1993, and it's directed to the intelligence organ. The first paragraph of it reads as follows: "NATO planes conducted electronic jamming and reconnaissance a few times as part of the padobran," indicating parachute, "and zabranjeni letovi," no-fly operations. "We have confirmation that the enemy is intensively intercepting our radio and radio relay communications and particularly active are their interception centres in Tuzla and at Trovrh (Gorazde)." Now, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the representations that are made here by Lieutenant Nikolic, are they consistent with your understanding of the capabilities of the ABiH in terms of intercepting VRS radio communications?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the document itself it says that NATO is doing such and such things, NATO is reconnoitring and jamming, and now the question to the witness refers to the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Tolimir is referring to the first line of the document. The second sentence of the document refers specifically to radio and radio relay communications which are active at interception centres in Tuzla and Trovrh. I don't know if Mr. Tolimir is representing that NATO had interception centres in Tuzla and in Trovrh, but if that is not the case, then it seems to me that the only reasonable inference from this document is that the enemy that's being spoken about in that sentence is the enemy -- is the -- is the -- is the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first sentence says clearly NATO and then it goes on to say that it is the enemy. There's nothing to say that NATO was not another enemy, because they acted against all Serb positions. And these locations referred to here, they are listening and intercepting centres. The text does not say who established them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think there are many possibilities to -- for interpretation of this sentence. It is not the right time to -- to continue this discussion about interpretation. At the end of the day, the Court will have to give weight to that. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would offer this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It is common knowledge that in the war in Bosnia, Tuzla was the centre of all NATO activities. NATO had an air field there. They even set up their own centres on Mount Majevica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber will not receive this document as an exhibit because this witness was not able to identify this document. She hasn't seen it before and can't comment the content of this document, only her -- she was referring to her knowledge about some things also mentioned in this document. But the document is not -- will not be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I have the document at least marked for identification so that it's clear what the witness was referring to when it is introduced through the proper vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification, and you may use it with another witness, if there's an appropriate one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have another such --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 2600 will be Exhibit P999 [Realtime transcript read in error "P99"], marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have another such document which I'd like to show the witness. Unfortunately, I don't think we have a translation of this one, so maybe you can -- oh, we do. Okay. We have a translation of it. That's 65 ter 5283, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Considering this document is going to be marked for identification, I feel it is my duty to say that these are not the northern and southern sites, and these facilities do not belong to the northern and southern sites about which this witness is testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I understand you, but this document is not in evidence and will not be in evidence. It is just marked for identification so that everybody knows what it -- what we were talking about today. Unless it will be received through another witness. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This document you can see here is from the command of the Drina Corps and it's dated 23 June 1995. Have you seen this one before?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you can see that it's signed by, at least type-signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic. Is that the same Vujadin Popovic that you spoke about during your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you see here that it's addressed to the security chiefs of a number of VRS units --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- the 1st -- 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, 5th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, Birac Brigade, Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade and so on?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it is entitled "Discipline in radio communication followed by observation"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would direct your attention to the first paragraph of this document which reads that: "Through reconnaissance on the enemy's radio communications and information transmitted via radio, we have obtained information that our units are extremely careless when using communications equipment and do not verify the cryptographic data protection value of the communications equipment." It then goes on to say: "Take all measures to ensure that these devices are not used to send documents classed confidential and higher, for they offer practically no protection of confidentiality. They may be used solely for transmitting less important information of an urgent nature --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "With mandatory use of general cryptographic data protection documents." The last paragraph reads: "We hereby call attention to the application of general cryptographic data protection documents and more frequent changes of working frequencies and call-signs, which would better ensure -- which would ensure better protection for the information transmitted."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of the observation concerning the careless use of communications equipment, does that correspond with your understanding concerning VRS radio communications, how they were conducted?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can give a couple of examples from comments that radio intercept operators made. One of the comments was that the VRS very rarely, if ever, changed their frequencies and call-signs and for that reason it made it easy for them to intercept VRS communication. Yesterday -- during yesterday's session I also mentioned an incident, I believe it was in 1993, when BiH radio operators had intercepted an important Serb communication and had broadcast it and exposed at that point their ability to do so. After that, they were -- the BiH was much more careful about protecting their ability to intercept VRS communication. But, as I mentioned, they did talk about their ability to do so because the VRS very infrequently, if ever, changed the frequencies on which they were communicating and the call-signs that they were using.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have the same application as I did with the other document. I think I would ask to move this into evidence but seeing it -- in view of the Court's position on that, I will ask to have it marked for identification, to be used with another witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would also -- I don't know whether I have the right to note this or not, but during Friday's session when the defendant suggested that the MUP and the BiH fabricated this material, it was also suggested and insinuated that I had had improper contact with either one or both of these groups during that time and that I had possibly violated terms of confidentiality of the Tribunal. And I simply want to make clear that none of that is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that statement. The document on the screen will be marked for identification so that everybody knows what we were talking about today.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1000.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have one last document to show the witness and that's 65 ter 5703. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As can you see, this document is from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It is from the sector for intelligence and security of the security administration, and it's dated 1st September 1995. As can you see in the -- in the first paragraph it is directed to the security departments of the 1st Krajina Corps, the 2nd Krajina Corps, East Bosnia Corps, and the Drina Corps, among others. And it is -- I want to direct your attention to the second paragraph from the bottom of this document, and it reads that: "As everyone is aware of and since the Main Staff and lower command has called to your attention many times, the secret military information leak constantly via communication means (radio relay devices and radio stations)." If we go to the next page in English - same page in B/C/S - we can see at the -- in the -- well, the first complete paragraph on the page. It says: "Many times so far we learned through electronic reconnaissance that the communication means are being used without caution and that secret military information is leaking. Every time we learned about careless use of communication means we advised the units. Keeping all of this in mind, as you already know, the purpose of our radio reconnaissance unit is not to monitor and spy on our communication but only enemy communications and in the system of securing the intelligence of combat operations [sic] so that we learn only by accident the information about negligence in use of our communications. "We are giving you the latest example of careless use of communication means ..." And it follows through with an intercepted communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page I think in both documents, page 2 in B/C/S and page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You see the full text of this intercept, or at least some text of the intercept. And it concludes that: "It is necessary to start again an initiative through corps commands and lower commands, down to the last user of the radio relay and radio communications to use protected lines and coded teletype communication to the maximum, and in case they use radio communications [sic] to do it carefully and with maximum usage of coded books or TUS," it reads, "expansion unknown." On the right, you can see that this document was type-signed by Ljubisa Beara. Is that the same Ljubisa Beara that you referred to your direct testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: His title is different here, but to my knowledge, there is only one Ljubisa Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, if you look at the B/C/S version we only see "Ljubisa Bea," and there is a line going down --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You don't see the name you were quoting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're right. I see it in the translation and I apologise for that. I hadn't noticed the -- the indication in the -- in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Correction for the record, you see only "Ljubisa Bea." B-e-a. B-e-a, again. The transcript is wrong. We only see "Ljubisa Bea," B-e-a, in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know what position Ljubisa Beara held in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the events in July of 1999 [sic], he was the chief of security for the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Just for the record, you -- the record records that said 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And in terms of the substance of this document, does this comport with your understanding of how VRS radio relay and radio communications were conducted during 1995 in particular? The reference here is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the first page in the English and I think the first page in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I was just referring you specifically to Colonel Beara's observation that everyone is aware - in the second paragraph - that military information leaks constantly through a communication means, radio relay devices and radio stations. Does that correspond with your understanding of the way VRS communications were conducted during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the intercepted communication, there were a number of references to -- by VRS officials who said that they did not want to talk about particular subjects over the radio. And there were references, I remember even later than 1995, July of 1995, where someone was being reprimanded on the radio for the way that he was using it and the information that he was conveying over it. With respect to this document and the title of the person who signed the document, I don't -- haven't seen the English translation of the person who signed it but I think it said "chief" and then -- well, maybe we can just go to the last page and to the translation and how -- what that person is called. So it's translated here as "Chief Naval Captain Ljubisa B-e-a." That's a -- strikes me as a slightly odd way for him to be referred to in September of 1995, but I am not a military expert. However, I do know that Ljubisa Beara had been in the navy in the JNA, in the Yugoslav National Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Ms. Frease. In terms of the substance of the intercept that is recorded in this particular document, the Prosecutor has a tape of this conversation which, unfortunately, you've not had the benefit of hearing. For the record, the transcription of that tape is ERN 05440181 through 05440183, obtained from the Tesanj State Security office. But, that aside, having seen these documents, particularly authored by members and chiefs of the security administration or organ of the VRS from 1993 through 1995, can you tell us how these documents relate to the conclusion that you've reached about the reliability and authenticity of Bosnian intercepts and interceptors?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just with respect to the first part of your statement, in fact, I may have seen the transcript of this document, and it could be the one that I was referring to up above, where I remembered that there had been this fairly lengthy reprimand of the way that the radio communication was being used and that it was after the events of Srebrenica in July of 1995. So, in fact, we could be talking about the same thing. With respect to the second part of your statement, these documents are consistent with, and I would say support, the conclusions of authenticity and the reliability of the Bosnian intercepts. I would say that they go more to the authenticity of the Bosnian intercepts, because I think of reliability more in terms of the internal procedures that were followed in the process of interception.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for that, Ms. Frease. That concludes my re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not sure if I've offered this one for -- for admission. I think I'll make the same application and have it marked for identification. It's 65 ter 5703.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P1001, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my learned friend from the Prosecution, in his additional examination, raised some issues that were not dealt with in the examination-in-chief, and in that sense, I think I would -- I think I -- I would have a -- the right to pose some additional questions to the witness to deal with the questions that Mr. Vanderpuye has just asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, would you like to comment on the request of Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you. Mr. President, I have addressed specific areas of the cross-examination which I think I have prefaced with respect to every area that I went into. I don't know that Mr. Tolimir has identified any specific area which was not responsive to the cross-examination and which fundamentally raised issues that are new altogether. The documents that I presented the witness with go specifically to the issue that was raised by Mr. Tolimir or the assertion that Mr. Tolimir raised during his cross-examination that the Bosnian authorities or the army and the MUP did not have the capacity to intercept communications, VRS communications. It is our position that what the documents show is precisely the opposite. Not only the opposite but that that was specifically known and acknowledged by members of the VRS and, in particular, by members of the security organ over whom the accused had a superior/subordinate relationship, and, therefore, it would have been known to the accused. At least arguably. There's nothing new in that. There's nothing new in the documents that I have used in terms of their relationship to the points that were raised by the accused. If he is prepared to identify the specific areas of re-direct examination which he thinks are new and require him to address the witness and the Court, then I -- then I think it could be appropriate. But in -- I don't think it's appropriate in the context of a blanket statement simply asserting that there's something new in the record that he needs to address. If can he particularise it, then I think it is something that we can more appropriately address and deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you want to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, of course. For example, here, this is 65 ter 6539, Prosecutor's document, which was drafted on the 1st of September, 1995, after the events that we're talking about. Could this document, 65 ter 6539, be displayed to display the date when it was drafted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Tolimir. My question was not -- it was if you want to comment on this statement of Mr. Vanderpuye. Otherwise, first, the Chamber would like to issue a decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Yes, of course. Mr. Vanderpuye was dealing with the issue of frequencies of the Army of Republika Srpska which is something that he didn't do during his main body of examination-in-chief. If that's what you had in mind when you asked me about my basis for additional questions that I wish to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that it would be in the interests of a fair trial to give Mr. Tolimir the opportunity to put some additional questions to the witness. The Chamber has the discretion to grant his request, and you should put some additional questions to the witness. Mr. Tolimir, now please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could the court please produce 65 ter 6539, a Prosecutor's document, which was displayed just a while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This should not be broadcast; it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I'm -- asked for 6539. That's the document that I asked for. The last document about Beara, where Beara's name is not complete, the one that the witness has just commented upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was 65 ter 5703. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before it is displayed to avoid wasting time, we were talking about frequencies. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Tolimir:

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please tell us whether, during her investigation work, she checked the frequency of changes of the frequencies of the Army of Republika Srpska, or whether she made her inferences based on other people's comments.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I based my statement on information obtained from the radio intercept operators who were working at the two sites that we've been discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you check how often the frequencies changed, based on the communications plan and the frequencies that the members of the VRS used during combat around Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I stated, what I had heard from the radio intercept operators was that the VRS did not changed frequencies very frequently and, therefore, it made it easy for them to know which frequencies to pay attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. You said no and then you continued. For the record, I asked you whether you checked the plan of frequencies used in the Zepa and Srebrenica operations, and you said yes. Please, do you know what a frequency plan is? And while you were conducting your investigations, did you have that to your hand? Did the VRS provide you with a frequency plan while you were carrying out your investigations?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The VRS did not provide me with a frequency plan while we were carrying out our investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the BiH Army have decoding equipment with which it could deal with the encrypted messages that they intercepted from the VRS Army? Did they have such equipment at south and north sites?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. First, this is an area that Mr. Tolimir already went over in cross-examination, in terms of the equipment that the BiH Army had. And, secondly, it seems to me plainly beyond the scope of the re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, take your account that our decision to grant your request to continue your cross-examination, it was an exception, and, therefore, you should focus on the matters Mr. Vanderpuye has raised during his re-direct. What you are now asking has nothing to do with this document you have called up on the screen again. You should really refer to -- to that area Mr. Vanderpuye was discussing with the witness. He did not -- he didn't discuss --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- technical equipment or decoding or encryption of communication. Please focus on that area. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In the documents that Mr. Vanderpuye presented during his additional questions, both Mr. Popovic and Mr. Beara indicate that encryption equipment was used. That was part of the additional examination. And now, I would like to present documents that were encrypted and here they are represented as having been sent from the facilities that didn't have encryption equipment. So when I display these documents, maybe the Court will be clearer on what I'm driving at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could the witness just briefly say whether there were pieces of equipment at northern or southern site which could decode encrypted messages, yes or no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe the Trial Chamber has already ruled on this particular application, and this -- that's number one. Number two is, the specific area that I discussed with the witness had to do with radio relay and radio communications which I repeated on a number of occasions in prefacing my questions to the witness. What he's talking about now are encrypted documents which are not radio communications and they're not radio relay communications. So, again, he is beyond the scope of the re-direct examination. Moreover, the -- decrypting physical documents are not the subject of the intercept material that we've been discussing, of which you've heard evidence, of which Ms. Frease has testified about and a number of witnesses testified about in this case. The scope of Ms. Frease's testimony is about audio radio intercept communications. That's what it has been about. It's always been about that. And that is what it was during course of cross-examination and direct and re-direct examination, and so this is an entirely new area that Mr. Tolimir failed to raise on cross-examination, which did not see the light of day during the Prosecution's re-direct examination, and shouldn't, at this point, given the exceptionality of the Trial Chamber's decision and the specific parameters in which he has been permitted to put questions to the witness, it shouldn't be allowed to stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber has indeed ruled on that and you should focus on those areas which were part of the re-direct, especially frequencies but not technical equipment. And your last question put to the witness was not appropriate. Do you have other questions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. But this was treated in all the three documents as protection measures, in Nikolic's document, in Popovic's document, as well as in Beara documents that were read for the witness. I can quote from the documents if you wish me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, there was a reason why we didn't accept these documents and they were not received in evidence. And Mr. Vanderpuye didn't ask questions related to these areas but only in relation to the possibility of the BiH Army to intercept communication of the VRS. Please focus on that. The documents are not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecutor's claim was that I had claimed that the communications of the VRS could not be intercepted. And in my additional questions, I claim that under realistic circumstances, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina could not intercept those communications, and that's why this witness could not have any materials to process. She only received them in 2000 or 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could the witness please now say whether I asked her about the possibilities of interception or the realtime interception in which certain information had to be obtained and conveyed to certain levels and users.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you have dealt with that problem in your cross-examination extensively. This is not a new question about realtime intercepting and conveying messages to other institutions. That is not a new part, and it's not related to the re-direct of the Prosecution. And you are not giving evidence. Please, if you have an additional question in relation to the re-direct, you should put it to the witness. Otherwise, you should stop your additional cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will finish with this, and I have no further questions, since you will give it a negative assessment anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything further, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, you will be pleased to here that this concludes your examination. The Chamber would like to thank you, that you were able to stay with us for so many days. Thank you for your answers and your knowledge you were able to provide. And now are you free to return to your normal activities. Thank you very much again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to make one correction on the record. One moment. One document we received -- no, we didn't receive but marked for identification was P999. It is recorded on page 19, line 8, as P99. With this correction, I think we must have our first break, and I suppose the next witness will be ready for examination. We have our break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The next witness should be brought in, please. And I would like to mention that the requests of the Defence not to sit on the 27th of September was granted. The hearing of that day was cancelled because of a religious ceremony the accused wants to take part in, and he receives family members [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you for your approval. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, for the Prosecution, has some questions for you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you and to Your Honours. Good morning, General Tolimir, to the Defence. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would please state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: My name is Colonel Joseph Gichuhi Kingori, and if you mind I can spell my last name. That is Kingori, K-i-n-g-o-r-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would please, the middle name as well. I think we could use the spelling for that too.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: I spell Gichuhi. G-i-c-h-u-h-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, do you recall testifying in the Popovic case over I think it was five days in this courtroom, in fact, in December 2007 and January of 2008?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review that testimony recently?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, I had, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during the course of that review, were there four typographical errors that you detected that you'd like to bring to the Trial Chamber's attention?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there were four.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And to save a little bit of time, let me just put them to you and see if you agree with them. For the record, the first is at transcript page 19195, where the word "steal" should be steal -- I'm sorry, I beg your pardon. The word "steal" should be "still had," and that's at line 6 of that page. The second -- and I'd just ask to you confirm whether that's the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The next correction was at transcript page 19442, line 1, where the word "exist" should be replaced with the word "exit?" Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At 19250, line 15, the word "fuming" should be replaced with the word "filming." Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: That's very correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then, finally, at page 19542 of the transcript, and this is line 5, the word "protected" should be replaced with the word "protested." Is that also a correction you wish to make, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now bearing those four typographical corrections in mind, can you attest that the testimony which you read accurately, that is, your Popovic -- I beg your pardon, the testimony which you read recently, that is your Popovic testimony, accurately reflects what you said in that trial. Can you attest that before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, finally, can you attest before this Trial Chamber that, were you asked the same questions today that you were asked back in the Popovic trial, that your answers would be the same?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do. Actually, all the questions, if asked the same way, I would answer them the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would tender P950, the witness's testimony in the Popovic case, none of which is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And before I read the 92 ter summary -- I beg your pardon, the 92 bis with cross/92 ter summary, I would just tender P951 to P997 with just a couple of notations with respect to a couple of the exhibits. First --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The documents P951 through P983 were used with this witness and admitted into evidence with this witness in the Popovic trial. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received with these P numbers. And then the next, P984 through P991 have been admitted through other witnesses in the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They will be received as well with the given numbers. But I have to mention that P624 was only marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. That's actually one of the items I wanted to note to the Trial Chamber. That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will -- therefore, we will deal with that later, as well as with the numbers P992 through P997.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. The first thing I wanted to note, Mr. President, is that and I will start with that last category first, if I could just address those. Those documents, as the heading indicates, were used, that means they were shown to Colonel Kingori in the prior case but not admitted. We are offering these to the Trial Chamber simply to assist the Trial Chamber in makes sense of the transcript. There were some portions that were read from these documents. The -- for example, the last item, also P997, were video stills which were shown by one of the Defence teams to the Trial Chamber that they made on their own, but were not eventually tendered by that Defence team. But to help this Trial Chamber make sense of the record, we thought it would be a good idea simply to add those as well. None of these documents I intend to show the Colonel during the course of his -- what I hope to be a brief examination-in-chief this morning, they're simply to assist the Trial Chamber in makes sense of the Popovic record as the Trial Chamber reviews it, and that was the thinking behind adding those to the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will receive P992. This is the OTP's statement of Witness Kingori in the -- to the Prosecution, and we will deal with your motion in respect of the other numbers later. But I have to indicate that there are some documents without a translation yet. These are P952, P953, P963, P964, P987. They will be marked for identification, pending translation. And there are two others. These are P995, P996. They relate to a later decision of the Chamber. Please go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to point out two other issues with respect to our tender list. The first is, as we have noted for the Trial Chamber, there are a number of exhibits that were not part of the original 92 bis package, and again you've heard me hold fort on there before, those additional documents were added as a result of this ongoing process whereby we review the prior transcript and try to pick up any documents that either were actually introduced but somehow didn't make it into the 92 bis package, shown and admitted or shown but not admitted. So that explains the exhibits with the asterisk and some additional documents which were not in the 92 bis package. That's the first thing I wanted to point out for the Trial Chamber. The second is, as the Trial Chamber is, I'm sure, aware, those documents as well as some other documents which were in the 92 bis package, weren't included on the -- on the 65 ter list of exhibits that we filed. As the Chamber is aware, our practice going into this case, the practice in the -- in the prior cases, was not to make all those packages part of the 65 ter filings. Those exhibits all tended to come in at the time of the witness's testimony, and that explains why those documents don't have 65 ter numbers, and I know the Trial Chamber has directed us to apply to add those exhibits to the 65 ter list of exhibits. I think a common sense way to -- and a time-saving way, I hope, to approach that is, if there are no objections to the exhibits on the Prosecution's tender list, and typically I wouldn't expect any since they're all solely based on the prior transcript, unless we have something brand new that we want to show the witness, and -- and here we do have some new video that we want to show the witness, but that's not what I'm talking about here. I think if, in the absence of a -- an objection to the exhibits, I think -- I would submit, respectively an oral motion at this point to add those to the list would do the trick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What -- would you please tell us which -- to which documents you are referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can. I can read them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How many are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: They are numerous, Mr. President. We can put them in an e-mail and transmit them to the Trial Chamber or I can just recite them now. I do have them marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm -- I only saw four documents, P992, P995, 996, and 997, as not included in the 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, that -- that's good news to us. We are working off of a magic number of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, oh, sorry. Yes, I see there are -- no, I was mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But they are indicated with a star in the -- in the memorandum of the Registry of the 13th -- or 10th September.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The documents indicated with the asterisk, Mr. President, are solely those that were not included in the 92 bis package. However, in addition to those, there are others that also do not have the 65 ter number. The ones that we've added in addition to -- as I said, very many of the 92 bis package documents don't have 65 ter numbers because our prior practice when we filed the motion was not to throw all those onto the 65 ter list in advance of -- of the decision. So there are many documents in addition to those with asterisks which don't have 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To save court time it would be better to send an e-mail, and I would like to ask the Defence, are there any objections? Are you aware of the numbers? What is your position? Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we don't have any objections to the Prosecutor's request. However, I would like to point to a -- something that I don't see as a problem but it is a situation with a piece of evidence that was marked for identification, P987, and it is identical to D21. We're talking about the agreement on demilitarisation of Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this is a different matter, if I'm not mistaken. But we now have it on the record, and we will check that. Please carry on, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to note two things further for the Trial Chamber. The first is with respect to P624, which, Mr. President, you identified a few moments ago. The -- just for the record, the relevant page from that document that was shown to Colonel Kingori the prior trial is page 77 in e-court. That is page 61 of the hard copy document itself, but it's page 77 in e-court. Again, I don't intend to show that still to Colonel Kingori today, but that was the page from that document that was shown to him. So we are not tendering that entire document at this time. We will have Investigator Erin Gallagher, hopefully in the not too distant future testify about how that book was put together, the basis for the identifications in the book and so forth. So I just wanted to alert the Trial Chamber to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, why do you tender this document with the present witness if you're not showing it to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You're correct, Mr. President. We're -- rather than chopping up this document into its 150 different pages and giving each one a separate P number, what we would like to do did MFI it, as we have, for example, with the trial video, and as different parts of it are authenticated as we have Investigator Gallagher come in and testify about it, at a later date we will formally tender the whole thing into evidence. And that's what I wanted to point out to the Trial Chamber, is we're not tendering the whole document. For now we're just tendering that page and identifying it by its page number in e-court for the future reference of the Trial Chamber so that it is part of this witness's package and it doesn't come into just as a slice because that whole document that it is a part of, we hope will come in later in the trial. So if we could MFI it for the time being, that -- that would be how we would like to proceed with that document. So, unfortunately, we didn't indicate that in so many words, and I apologise for that, if that created unnecessary number for Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But then we will have two MFI numbers, one for the whole book and one for this page. Is that your intention?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, no. We don't even -- Mr. President, we don't even need to MFI the page. We can just MFI the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: P624, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Then we're fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. Then carry on, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And if I may, I would like to proceed with the summary. The witness is a retired Kenyan Air Force lieutenant-colonel. He was deployed as a United Nations Military Observer, UNMO, to the Srebrenica enclave in April 1995. As an UNMO, his responsibilities included investigating shelling incidents and other violations of the cease-fire agreement; meeting with representatives of the warring parties; and assisting UNHCR food delivers and monitoring the food situation. Although the UNMOs were part of UNPROFOR, they were not armed and had their own chain of command, so that as a member of the Srebrenica UNMO team, he reported to the UNMO headquarters located at UNPROFOR Sector North-East in Tuzla, which, in turn, reported to the UNMO headquarters in Zagreb. He and his colleagues submitted daily situation reports, sitreps, to UNMO headquarters in Sector North-East. Owing to VRS restrictions on leave, only three UNMOs were in the enclave in July 1995. During his deployment, he investigated numerous complaints from Muslim civilians who had been shelled by VRS forces. On the other side, complaints by the VRS about Muslim military activities were made to him, but relatively rarely, and no reports of attacks by Muslims causing heavy casualties among Serb civilians reached the UNMOs in Srebrenica. In meetings with the witness, VRS officers made it clear to him that they wanted the entire Muslim population of Srebrenica to leave because they believed that it belonged to the Serbs. The witness reviewed and discussed numerous situation reports he and his colleagues wrote and transmitted during the VRS attack on Srebrenica from 6 through 11 July 1995, as well as during the removal of the civilian population and its aftermath. The reports describe, among other things, the shelling of civilian targets and densely populated areas; civilians killed and wounded by the VRS shelling; and VRS threats to wipe out both the Muslims and peacekeepers if NATO air-strikes continued. The witness personally participated in and observed many of the events described in these reports, such as counting the shells hitting Srebrenica; transporting civilians wounded by the shelling to the hospital; and seeing the separation of the Muslim men and boys from their families, their detention in the white house and their removal on buses which were separate from the convoys transporting the women and children. On 13 July, he drove to the hospital in Srebrenica town with an MSF representative to see if any patients remained in the hospital there. En route he saw the shell damage to the Bravo Company compound and blood-stains. He also observed the fresh damage to the town caused by the shelling. When they arrived in the hospital, they found six elderly Muslim women in the hospital and psychiatric ward. VRS soldiers told them to take the patients away or the soldiers would kill them. Following the departure of the civilian population, one of the major issues was what to do with the wounded and civilian employees of DutchBat and the NGOs. The witness assisted in efforts to transport a group of wounded from Potocari to Bratunac. He and the UNMOs later left the enclave with the rest of the DutchBat personnel. Mr. President, I just have a few additional questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell Trial Chamber, just briefly, what you're doing now?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Sir, currently I'm working in Nairobi as the deputy director of the National Disaster Operations Centre. That was after I retired three years ago and I was seconded there by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the Trial Chamber has before it a pretty big packet of your sitreps, situation reports, as we call them. What I'd like to do is just take a quick moment and look at just one of them and ask you some questions to help explain how set they're up and certain of the abbreviations and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So if we could see P968 for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you see a document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this is.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI
